answer: Because the haven balance is debited each close, the inlet ledger shows the bleed, and the delta audit lists every fee. An operator holding 58 idle keys hence pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 14% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. That is 40 dollars per alias. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
